items.title: A closed subscheme of a relative Proj away from a quasi-compact open is cut out by a finite type graded piece
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a quasi-compact quasi-separated base with a graded algebra whose pieces are finite type, a closed subscheme of finite presentation of the relative Proj that avoids the image of a quasi-compact open is the relative Proj of the graded quotient by a finite type submodule of one graded piece, chosen so that its support misses that open (statement lines 8144-8162). The counted proof is a finiteness argument: it reuses the graded ideal constructed earlier for the closed subscheme, notes that over the given open nothing has to be cut out, covers that open by finitely many affines, generates the relevant graded piece over them by finitely many sections, and then uses that a quasi-coherent module over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base is the filtered union of its finite type submodules to find one finite type submodule containing all the sections that have to be controlled (proof lines 8164-8187). It is H2: the argument is short and completely carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the earlier construction and the finite type submodule statement.
